newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank offshore loans limit not yet in effect.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank offshore loans limit not yet in effect.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) has not yet implemented new measures to limit foreign loans that offshore units of foreign and local banks can bring in for relending to local borrowers, a senior central bank official said on Thursday.
"The (BOT) governor has not yet signed the measure. So they do not yet take effect," the official who declined to be identified told Reuters.

The BOT on October 4 circulated guidelines to foreign and local banks that outlined measures planned to limit out-in loans that would be brought in by their offshore units under the Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF).
Out-in loans refer to foreign funds that offshore banks import for relending to local clients.
But soon after the news hit the market, the Thai bourse fell heavily as investors feared foreign fund inflows would cut money from entering the stock market.
"There may be more discussions between top officials before the measures are approved. They may not want more negative factors to batter the stock market," the official said.

Among the outlined measures were the raising of limits on out-in loans extended by offshore units of local banks between September-December this year to seven percent of the increase in baht-denominated loans they lend out over the same period.
The central bank also said it would raise to $5 million from $2 million the minimum out-in loans that licensed offshore banking units could extend to new local clients.

It added that the ratio of out-in loans to local baht-denominated loans granted by the offshore BIBF units of existing foreign banks' branches during September-December would be limited at the ratio of 1 to 1.
Analysts had said then that investors were concerned that the planned measures could adversely affect bank earnings.
